authoring_quiz.title: Module 1 Quiz: Introduction to Apache Doris
authoring_quiz.description: Six questions check the workload, architecture, and first-workflow decisions of Module 1, one question for each learning objective.

questions.objective: Define Apache Doris as an open-source, real-time analytics and search database built on an MPP architecture.
questions.prompt: Which statement best describes Apache Doris?

options.text: A BI application that stores the charts and dashboards of analysts
An object storage service that keeps Parquet files for query engines
An open-source real-time analytics and search database with MPP execution
A row-oriented transactional database with an analytical plug-in for reports

questions.explanation: Doris is an open-source, real-time analytics and search database built on an MPP architecture: it stores data in columns and runs analytical queries in parallel. A BI tool and an object store can work with Doris, but neither one is Doris, and Doris is not a transactional database with an analytical add-on.

questions.objective: Distinguish OLAP from OLTP by the work that a request does, not by the product that runs it.
questions.prompt: Which request is the clearest example of an OLAP workload?

options.text: Update the delivery address of one order and commit the change
Scan 100 million events and total the revenue by region and hour
Look up the current payment token of one checkout session by its key
Reserve one unit of a product for a cart and commit the transaction

questions.explanation: The revenue request scans and aggregates many records, which is the work of an analytical workload. Updating one address, looking up one token by its key, and reserving one unit each touch a single business entity in a small transaction, which is the work of OLTP, whichever product runs it.

questions.objective: Recognize workloads that suit Doris, such as real-time dashboards, customer-facing analytics, observability, lakehouse analytics, and CDC-driven reporting.
questions.prompt: An ecommerce company must keep its OLTP database as the system of record, but its dashboards need committed order changes within seconds, without running large scans on that database. Which design fits best?

options.text: Run every dashboard aggregation directly against the OLTP database
Export a full snapshot of the OLTP database to Doris once each night
Copy the changed rows into object storage files without a query engine
Deliver committed changes to Doris continuously through CDC

questions.explanation: Change data capture keeps the operational database responsible for transactions and delivers each committed change to Doris, where the dashboards run their analytical queries. Scanning the OLTP database adds analytical load to it, a nightly snapshot is a day old, and files without a query engine do not answer the dashboards.

questions.objective: Summarize what the Frontend (FE) and the Backend (BE) each do with a query.
questions.prompt: Which description follows a query through Doris correctly?

options.text: The BE creates the distributed plan, and the FE executes each plan fragment
The MySQL client plans the query, and the FE and BE only store replicas
The FE plans the query and assigns its fragments; the BE nodes execute them
The FE renders charts in a browser, and the BE turns the charts into SQL

questions.explanation: The FE accepts and analyzes the SQL, creates and optimizes the distributed query plan, and assigns its plan fragments; the BE nodes execute the fragments and, in the integrated architecture, also store the table data. The roles are not reversed, the client only sends SQL, and "Frontend" does not mean a graphical interface.

questions.objective: Distinguish the integrated storage and compute architecture from the decoupled storage and compute architecture.
questions.prompt: A team wants its persistent data in shared object storage, and separate compute groups that scale independently and isolate workloads. Which architecture matches these requirements?

options.text: The decoupled storage and compute architecture
The integrated storage and compute architecture
A read replica of the transactional database
Parquet files in object storage, queried without Doris

questions.explanation: In the decoupled storage and compute architecture, persistent data lives in shared storage, and compute groups scale and isolate workloads independently. In the integrated architecture, stateful BE nodes store the data on local disks, so storage and compute grow together. A transactional read replica and bare files offer neither.

questions.objective: Connect to Doris through its MySQL-compatible protocol, create a table, load data, and check the result with an aggregation query.
questions.prompt: In Lab 1, INSERT INTO events SELECT ... FROM S3(...) reports 10,158,080 affected rows. Which check shows what the internal table events now holds?

options.text: Query COUNT(*), MIN(event_time), and MAX(event_time) from events
Run the S3 TVF query with LIMIT 10 again and compare its ten rows
Run SHOW BACKENDS and check that the BE reports Alive = true
Check that docker ps shows the doris-rta container as healthy

questions.explanation: The insert reports what one statement wrote; a query of the table shows what it now holds: 10,158,080 rows from 2019-12-01 00:00:12 to 2020-03-11 04:53:08, the values that Lab 1 checks. The S3 TVF reads the files in S3, not the table, and SHOW BACKENDS and the container's health show that Doris runs, not what the table contains.
